title: Controller & View — One Fact, Four Checkpoints (Set 2)
description: A second mastery pass on the same Controller-View core fact, approached through new scenarios: stacked views, captured output, broken flows, and the full round trip.
coreFact: The Controller receives the request, runs the logic, and calls $this->load->view() to hand data to a View, which renders the HTML. Logic stays in the Controller; presentation stays in the View.
congratsText: Four new angles, same one truth — the Controller drives, the View displays.
objectives: Explain how a Controller can load several Views in sequence to build one page
Choose between sending a View to the browser and capturing it as a string
Diagnose a request flow that fails because the Controller never loaded a View
Trace the full round trip from URL to rendered HTML and back
recap: A Controller may call the view loader several times, and the output stacks in call order
Passing TRUE as the third argument returns the View's HTML as a string instead of sending it
A blank page usually means the Controller method ran but never loaded a View
The round trip is always URL to Controller to logic to View to HTML back to the browser

chunks.text: A Controller can call the view loader more than once, which is how a page gets a shared header and footer.

check.question: How many Views can one Controller method load?

chunks.text: The output stacks in call order — the header View must be loaded before the body View.

check.question: What decides the order of the output?

chunks.text: Each loaded View still only knows the data the Controller passed to it on that particular call.

check.question: Does a View see data passed to a different View?

quiz.question: Arrange the Controller lines so the page renders header, then content, then footer.

chunks.text: By default the view loader sends the rendered HTML straight into the response the browser receives.

check.question: By default, where does the HTML go?

chunks.text: Passing TRUE as the third argument makes the loader return that HTML as a string instead.

check.question: What does the third argument TRUE do?

chunks.text: Either way the Controller stays in charge — it decides whether the markup is sent or stored.

quiz.question: What does $html contain after this line runs?
options: The rendered HTML of the invoice View, as a string
A reference pointing back to the invoice View file on disk
The $data array exactly as it was passed into the view loader
Nothing, because the markup was already flushed to the browser

chunks.text: If a Controller method runs but never loads a View, the browser receives a blank page, not an error.
An Unable to load error instead means the filename in the loader does not match any file in the views folder.

check.question: That error points to a problem with the what?

chunks.text: An undefined variable notice inside a View means the Controller forgot to pass that key.

check.question: Who forgot to supply the variable?

quiz.question: Visiting this Controller shows a completely blank page. Why?
options: The method never loads a View, so nothing is rendered
The query returned no rows, so the page had nothing at all to display
The $data array was never converted into individual page variables first
The method name index is reserved and cannot produce any output at all

chunks.text: Every request starts at a URL that routing maps onto one Controller method.

check.question: What does routing map a URL to?

chunks.text: That method gathers whatever it needs, then calls the loader to hand off to a View.
The View turns that data into HTML, and the response travels back to the browser.

quiz.question: In one word, name the part of the round trip that runs the logic and decides which View to load.
